No source states a specific 'first proposed in <year>' date distinct from either the c.2000 first-attempt year (already recorded on the sheet as ConstructionYear) or the 2007 restart year. Rather than arbitrarily pick one of these as 'Proposal' or duplicate ConstructionYear, leaving ProposalYear/ProposalMonth UNRESOLVED with this history recorded for whoever revisits it.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Sheet records Capacity=18.60 with CapacityUnits='mtpa'. This is a gas TRANSMISSION PIPELINE, not an LNG plant, so mtpa (mass throughput, the LNG-plant unit) is the wrong unit family; the controlled vocabulary for a gas pipeline's design throughput is bcm/y (billion m3/year). energypolicy.ru (Wayback capture, verified) states explicitly: 'транссахалинский магистральный газопровод ... Протяженность трассы газопровода – 637 км, диаметр – 1220 мм, проектная мощность – 18,6 млрд м3/год' (design capacity 18.6 billion m3/year — i.e. bcm/y). The SAME article separately states the Sakhalin-2 LNG PLANT's output as '9,6 млн т/год' (9.6 million tonnes/year = 9.6 mtpa). en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakhalin-II independently corroborates the LNG plant figure as '9.6 million tonnes ... per year'. So GEM's sheet appears to have taken the correct numeral (18.6, the pipeline's own bcm/y design capacity) but mislabeled its unit as mtpa — possibly by analogy/confusion with the LNG plant's separate 9.6 mtpa figure. The number 18.6 does NOT match the LNG plant's 9.6 mtpa under any obvious conversion, and does match the pipeline's own stated design throughput as bcm/y exactly. Filing as a spec/unit concern rather than silently changing CapacityUnits, per SOP (contested surfaces the exact backend column + proposed value for human review).

The row's entire traceable basis is a single 2018 news-media infographic that GEM's own page says shows the line only as 'prospective' and explicitly absent from Gazprom's own 2019 Annual Report; no independent Russian-language or English-language source (Gazprom, Sakhatransneftegaz, Sakha Republic government, Glavgosexpertiza, neftegaz.ru, TASS, Interfax, regional Yakutia press) names a distinct 'Yakutsk-Aldan' gas pipeline project. resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's own P2706 wiki page (read for leads only, never cited) carries exactly TWO harvested citations and states its entire case in one paragraph: 'A pipeline running from Yakutsk to Aldan is shown as a "prospective gas pipeline" on a Financial Times graphic from April 3, 2018. However, it is not shown on the Gazprom 2019 Annual Report... As of July 2022, there have been no further news about this project, and it appears to be cancelled.' So GEM's cite #1 (Gazprom 2019 Annual Report PDF, gazprom.com) is cited to document an ABSENCE, not a confirmation, and GEM's cite #2 is the FT interactive graphic accompanying 'Russia's $55bn pipeline gamble on China's demand for gas' (ig.ft.com/gazprom-pipeline-power-of-siberia/) -- the SAME article whose headline figure is almost certainly the source of the implausible $55bn SegmentCost already flagged as a likely aggregate-cost defect on sibling row P2352 (Power of Siberia Phase I), i.e. this exact graphic is already known in this batch to be a source of miscalibrated/aggregated figures, not a primary engineering document. I could not independently view the graphic itself: ig.ft.com returned an HTTP 302 (subscription wall) to a plain curl and WebFetch refused the ft.com domain outright, so I cannot confirm what the graphic's 'Yakutsk-Aldan' label actually depicts or whether it is a genuine standalone route versus a simplified regional label. Ran extensive Russian-language searches for a dedicated project ('газопровод Якутск Алдан', '"Якутск-Алдан" трубопровод проект') across Russian news, government and trade-press indexes: found nothing naming a distinct Yakutsk-Aldan gas pipeline. What DOES exist near Aldan is different infrastructure: Gazprom's South/West Yakutia gasification programme taps the Power of Siberia trunk (P2352/P2353) with four short branch pipelines (газопроводы-отводы) feeding gas-distribution stations (ГРС) 'Aldan', 'Aldan-2', 'Мурья' and 'Чульман' (neftegaz.ru, yakutia.info, yakutia-daily.ru, yk24.ru, Sept 2026 reporting) -- local distribution spurs OFF the Power of Siberia trunk near where it already passes through Aldan district, not a 466 km trunk originating at Yakutsk city. Critically, Yakutsk city itself is not on the Power of Siberia route at all (that trunk runs Chayanda field/Lensky district -> Aldan/Olekminsk/Neryungri districts -> Amur Oblast, well south of Yakutsk); Yakutsk's own gas supply comes from the wholly separate Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk system, already recorded as 8 other rows on this same roster (P2334, P3361, P3364, P3365, P6691, P6694, P6695, P6696). A direct ~466 km gas trunk connecting Yakutsk city to Aldan town therefore does not correspond to any real gas corridor I could find any evidence of -- it reads as a plausible misreading of a simplified news graphic rather than a documented engineering project. I checked the 32-row Far East roster for a possible relabeled duplicate (e.g. a segment of P2352/P2353 or one of the Aldan-area feeder rows P6682/P3896/P6710/P7600) but none matches this row's stated termini (Yakutsk city -> Aldan district) closely enough to call it the same physical entity under another name, so I am not filing a duplicate flag -- existence is the primary open question, not misattribution to a sibling PID. resolutions.recommendation: Adjudicate against P5521 (Belogorsk-Khabarovsk Gas Pipeline, Svobodny->Khabarovsk Territory, 828 km, status=construction). Both rows track the same physical corridor: a connector linking the Power of Siberia (Chayanda-sourced) system to the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok (Sakhalin-sourced) system across Amur Oblast, the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, and Khabarovsk Krai. energypolicy.ru's 2024 academic account gives the actual history: a Belogorsk(Amur Oblast)-Birobidzhan(JAO)-Khabarovsk extension WAS part of Power of Siberia-1's ORIGINAL design (when PoS-1 was planned to run Chayanda->Vladivostok with an LNG plant there); it was 'set aside' ('otoshel na vtoroy plan') once Gazprom instead routed China-bound gas directly via Blagoveshchensk (the trunk actually built, 2019). That shelved concept is very likely what GEM staged as P3208 ('Phase I Expansion', Blagoveshchensk->Khabarovsk Krai, cancelled) -- existence and the 'cancelled' framing are independently corroborated (see status_reviews). BUT the SAME corridor has since 2022 been revived under the name 'MG Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' (830 km per energypolicy.ru, matching GEM's own P5521 at 828 km) as part of the 'Eastern Gas Supply System' (Vostochnaya sistema gazosnabzheniya / VSG), officially listed alongside Power of Siberia-2 in the Russian government's 16-Nov-2024 decree No. 3302-r (legalacts.ru) covering Gazprom's mandated trunk-pipeline construction program, target completion 2029 (prokhab.ru, eastrussia.ru, both Oct 2022). Recommendation: either (a) merge P3208 into P5521 if GEM intends one continuous project record (revived project inherits the corridor), or (b) if GEM's convention is to retain the original shelved 1st-generation concept as its own row, then P3208's segment name/notes should say explicitly that it is the PRE-2022 discontinued precursor to the corridor now tracked as P5521, so a researcher does not read the two rows as unrelated pipelines or double-count 620+828=1448 km of corridor that is physically one ~800-830 km route. Whichever way this is resolved, P3208's own LengthKnown/Capacity numbers (620 km / 32 bcm/y) are NOT supported by any source found for either the original or the revived concept -- see the spec concern below.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Read to exhaustion: prokhab.ru (Wayback, Oct 2022, Khabarovsk krai governor's press service), eastrussia.ru (Wayback, Oct 2022, same underlying announcement -- these two are ONE origin, both relaying the governor's press service), energypolicy.ru (independent academic journal article, 2024, a genuinely separate origin with its own historical analysis), and neftegaz.ru + legalacts.ru (Nov 2024, reporting/quoting the actual government decree -- a third independent origin, official record). All four together: 3 independent origins corroborating that (1) a Belogorsk/Amur Oblast-to-Khabarovsk connector was part of PoS-1's original routing and was shelved, and (2) the same corridor concept, ~830 km, is now an active government-mandated construction project named 'Belogorsk-Khabarovsk', which is what P5521 already tracks. Checked P5521 is not itself sourced from these same documents in the current sheet (P5521 carries no [ref] per the roster's MISSING_REF/MISSING_VALUE pattern implied by the batch calibration), so this is new evidence for that row too -- filed as a cross_row_lead.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and extensively documented. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 32-row roster's 8-row Sakhatransneftegaz Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk family (P3365, P6695, P3361, P3364, P6691, P2334, P6696, P6694): P3361 is specifically the 84km Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh THIRD line, distinct in name, length, and build era from every sibling checked this run -- it is NOT the same object as the older Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk corridor (382km per family notes; a 2019 neftegaz.ru incident report on that OLDER, then-51-year-old pipe at km 239 is a different, much longer-established segment -- see the attribution flag below, which explains why that article is a bad Capacity ref for THIS row despite superficially overlapping names) nor the Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk lines (P2334/P6696, a wholly separate 1960s-era corridor). resolutions.researcher_notes: neftegaz.ru/194257 states: 'Проектная производительность 2-х ниток - 4,2 млн м3/сутки, максимальная - 6,3 млн м3/сутки, 3-й нитки - около 8 млн м3/сутки.' On balance the per-thread reading is favored and supports the recorded value at medium confidence.

resolutions.recommendation: No change to existence/classification. P5521 is a real, actively-progressing project: a ~828-830 km gas transmission bridge from the Amur Gas Processing Plant at Svobodny (Amur Oblast), through Birobidzhan (Jewish AO), to a tie-in with the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok trunk near Khabarovsk, built as Stage 1 of Gazprom's 'Eastern Gas Supply System' (Vostochnaya sistema gazosnabzheniya, VSG). Independently corroborated by interfax.ru (national wire, quoting Gazprom's own annual-report language), the Khabarovsk Krai/Minenergo official statement via dfo.gov.ru, the general contractor Gazstroyprom's own project page (gsprom.ru), neftegaz.ru's technical-library system overview, and construction-progress reporting from portamur.ru (May 2026, 75% built) and akm.ru (Gazprom press-service mirror). See the duplicate, spec, and attribution concerns below for the caveats.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Read to exhaustion: interfax.ru/business/951688 (whole-VSG announcement article naming this segment specifically, 830 km, pressure spec, fuel-source language), gsprom.ru/projects/gas-trunklines/ (contractor's own project card, 828 km exact), dfo.gov.ru/press/news_DV/7942/ (27-May-2025 official Minenergo statement, 828 km, 2027 target), neftegaz.ru tech-library 830816 (VSG system overview, separates system-wide 'Характеристики проекта ВСГ' from Stage-1-specific 'перемычка' facts -- the source of the aggregate-vs-segment issues below), neftegaz.ru news 889825, akm.ru (Gazprom press-release mirror, April 2025, 1420mm/K70/150atm pipe spec + 356km progress), tek-all.ru (23-Apr-2026 independent overview, corroborates 1420mm diameter but gives a conflicting 9.8 MPa pressure figure), portamur.ru (03-May-2026, 75% built / 754 of 828 km), finance.rambler.ru (26-Jun-2026, Miller AGM commissioning announcement), prokhab.ru via Wayback (27-Oct-2022, dated dispatch confirming April-2022 presidential decision), energypolicy.ru via Wayback (2024 academic analysis of VSG spatial development). No evidence found anywhere describing a different, separate project at this location -- all Russian-language coverage converges on one continuous corridor and construction effort. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 0 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no; tier high -> medium (0 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s); a single source is medium at best).

resolutions.recommendation: Adjudicate P5521 against P3208 ('Power of Siberia Gas Pipeline' / 'Phase I Expansion' segment, Blagoveshchensk->Khabarovsk Krai, 620 km, 32 bcm/y, status=cancelled). A separate shard for P3208 staged in this same batch (rows/P3208.json) independently reached the identical conclusion from the other direction: both rows track the same physical corridor -- a connector linking the Power of Siberia (Chayanda-sourced) system to the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok (Sakhalin-sourced) system across Amur Oblast, the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, and Khabarovsk Krai. energypolicy.ru's 2024 academic account explains the lineage: a Belogorsk-Birobidzhan-Khabarovsk extension was part of Power of Siberia-1's ORIGINAL design (when PoS-1 was to run Chayanda->Vladivostok with an LNG plant there); it was shelved ('otoshel na vtoroy plan') once Gazprom instead routed China-bound gas directly via Blagoveshchensk (the trunk actually built, 2019) -- that shelved concept is very likely GEM's P3208. The SAME corridor was revived in 2022 (Presidential decision, April 2022, per prokhab.ru) under the name 'MG Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' (828-830 km, matching P5521 almost exactly) as VSG Stage 1, formally listed in the Russian government's 16-Nov-2024 decree No. 3302-r alongside Power of Siberia-2. Recommendation: either (a) merge/supersede P3208 into P5521 (the revived project inherits the corridor and P3208 becomes a historical alias), or (b) if GEM's convention is to keep the shelved first-generation concept as its own row, add an explicit note on P3208 that it is the pre-2022 discontinued precursor now tracked live as P5521, and drop or caveat P3208's own 620 km / 32 bcm/y figures -- no source (for either the original or revived concept) supports those numbers; every dated source gives ~800-830 km for this corridor, never 620 km.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Corroborated independently in this session via interfax.ru, dfo.gov.ru, neftegaz.ru, energypolicy.ru (Wayback), and prokhab.ru (Wayback) -- all naming 'Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' specifically at 828-830 km, never Blagoveshchensk-Khabarovsk at 620 km. The current ref (neftegaz.ru tech-library 830816) itself makes this explicit: the article structures the 28 bcm/y figure under a top-level 'Характеристики проекта ВСГ' (VSG PROJECT characteristics) block, separate from and above its own 'Стадия 1 проекта ВСГ: строительство газопровода-перемычки' (Stage 1: construction of the bridge pipeline = Belogorsk-Khabarovsk) block, which gives ONLY length (~830 km) and no capacity figure of its own. Recommend either removing Capacity/CapacityUnits from this segment-level row (leaving it to a project/system-level record if GEM tracks VSG at that level) or keeping it with an explicit ResearcherNotes caveat that 28 bcm/y is the full multi-thousand-km VSG target, not this bridge's own capacity.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Read the full neftegaz.ru article structure directly (not just a keyword hit): 'Характеристики проекта ВСГ протяженность: более 5000 км; пропускная мощность - 28 млрд м3/год... ресурсная база - месторождения, зарезервированные для МГП Северный поток 2; маршрут: полуостров Ямал, ХМАО, Томская область, Кемеровская область, Красноярский край и Иркутская область' -- this is explicitly the WHOLE-SYSTEM block. The very next section, '1 этап проекта ВСГ: строительство газопровода-перемычки', covers Belogorsk-Khabarovsk specifically and gives only the ~830 km figure, no capacity. This is exactly the aggregate-vs-segment pattern the batch is calibrated to catch. [QC] tier high -> medium (1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s); a single source is medium at best).

resolutions.recommendation: FuelSource='Yamal gas fields' is also a whole-VSG-system aggregate (the SAME neftegaz.ru article's system-level block lists 'ресурсная база - месторождения, зарезервированные для МГП Северный поток 2' / route 'полуостров Ямал, ХМАО...' -- gas that would need the yet-unbuilt WESTERN legs of VSG to ever reach this bridge). Recommend correcting FuelSource for this segment to 'Power of Siberia (Chayanda/Kovykta, Yakutia) and Sakhalin gas fields', with a note that Yamal is the aggregate future VSG-system resource base, not what feeds this specific bridge.

resolutions.recommendation: Keep as recorded -- real, distinct project; not a duplicate of any sibling Yakutia-gasification row.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Existence: strongly corroborated. This 207 km (recorded; 209 km per lenskrayon.ru, within normal route-vs-straight-line variance) gas transmission pipeline running from the Srednebotuobinskoye Gas and Condensate Field (Mirninsky District, Sakha Republic) to the Novolenskaya TES site near Lensk is documented across 9+ independent sources spanning 2023-2026: the RF Government's own Territorial Planning Scheme (sudact.ru, Decree 816-r as amended), the Lensk/Mirninsky-district municipal public-hearing notice (2025), the Alrosa-Gas press release (2023), two peretok.ru trade-press articles (Sept 2023, Feb 2024), a TASS article (Aug 2023), the pipeline design institute's own PDF (ipigaz.ru, 2024, giving exact 207.0 km / 530mm specs), energo-news.ru (Feb 2025, Glavgosexpertiza approval), neftegaz.ru (Apr 2025, pipe-delivery status sourced to Inter RAO), lenskrayon.ru (Jun 2024, on-the-ground construction-site report naming the same 209 km pipeline), and bigpowernews.ru/TASS (May 2026, SZPK investment-protection agreement explicitly covering 'more than 200 km of gas pipeline for the station's gas supply'). No phantom-entity risk. Classification: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both confirmed -- the ipigaz.ru design document classifies the 530x10mm pipe as 'газопровод I класса' under SP 36.13330.2012 (pressure class I, 2.5-10 MPa design pressure), which is GEM's transmission-tier classification, not a low-pressure distribution line. Duplicate-vs-roster: BRIEF.md flags four sibling Yakutia-gasification PIDs in this batch (P6710 Srednetyungskoye-Nakyn, P3896 Kysyl-Syr-Amga-Ayan, P2706 Yakutsk-Aldan, P7600) as the 'common document set' to check against. None of the sources opened for P6682 name or describe any of those four lines, their fields, or their route corridors -- this pipeline's field (Srednebotuobinskoye) and terminus (Novolenskaya TES/Lensk) are geographically and administratively distinct from all four (which serve the central Yakutia gasification programme around Yakutsk/Nakyn/Amga/Aldan, ~500+ km to the northeast). No overlap or redundancy found; no cross_row_lead needed on this axis.

resolutions.recommendation: Change Owner1 from 'Alrosa-Gas JSC' (100%) to 'Novolenskaya TES LLC' (OOO "Novolenskaya TES"), with a note that Novolenskaya TES LLC is itself 99.9%-owned by AO 'Inter RAO - Elektrogeneratsiya' (a PAO Inter RAO subsidiary) per EGRUL data reported in peretok.ru. Alrosa-Gas's documented role is building/operating the UKPG (gas treatment unit) AT the Srednebotuobinskoye field and the short local distribution line to it (per ipigaz.ru and alrosa.ru) -- a related but DIFFERENT asset from the >200 km trunk transmission pipeline (МГП) that carries gas onward to the Novolenskaya TES site, which multiple independent sources consistently attribute to the TES project sponsor, not Alrosa-Gas.
resolutions.researcher_notes: The recorded Owner1='Alrosa-Gas JSC' (100%) appears to conflate two distinct, adjacent assets. Alrosa-Gas (a joint venture/subsidiary tied to diamond miner Alrosa) is well-documented as the builder/owner of the gas-treatment facility (UKPG, установка комплексной подготовки газа) at the Srednebotuobinskoye field itself (alrosa.ru press release, 2023-09; peretok.ru/26813, 2023-09-06) and of local/short gas-distribution infrastructure per the ipigaz.ru design PDF (which separately lists a much shorter 1.37 km, 530x9mm 'gas distribution network' pipe alongside the 207 km, 530x10mm main line). But the 207-209 km TRUNK pipeline to Novolenskaya TES is repeatedly and consistently described, across 5 independent sources spanning 2024-2026, as part of the Novolenskaya TES project's own scope, funded/built by the TES developer -- NOT by Alrosa-Gas: (1) peretok.ru/27372 (2024-02-26, Wayback-verified): reports EGRUL ownership data for OOO 'Novolenskaya TES' showing AO 'Inter RAO - Elektrogeneratsiya' holding 99.9% of the entity that the article frames as responsible for the station AND its associated ~200 km gas-supply pipeline (the article explicitly separates 'технологическое присоединение к газовой инфраструктуре Алроса-Газ' [connection TO Alrosa-Gas's infrastructure] from the trunk-pipeline construction, i.e. Alrosa-Gas is the thing being CONNECTED TO, not the builder of the connecting trunk line). (2) lenskrayon.ru (2024-06-17, url_verifier ok:true, name_found:true): a Lensk-district on-site report quoting the Novolenskaya TES site director (Денис Покровский) describing active land clearing and pipe-product delivery 'на площадке строительства магистрального газопровода' as part of the TES construction project run by 'группой компаний «Интер РАО» по заданию Правительства РФ' (the Inter RAO group of companies, on assignment from the RF Government). (3) neftegaz.ru/886763 (2025-04-17, sourced to Inter RAO, url_verifier ok:true, name_found:true): explicitly separates Alrosa-Gas's UKPG-building role from the connecting МГП (trunk gas pipeline, >200 km), states most of the required pipe product has been delivered, and sources the project's completion-date guidance (2028 per Inter RAO's own site) to Inter RAO directly. (4) 1prime.ru (2026-08-06, RIA/PRIME wire, url_verifier ok:true, name_found:true): reports a 31%% cost increase to 337.7bn RUB for the Novolenskaya TES project, itemizing 'технологическое подключение... к газовой инфраструктуре Среднеботуобинского месторождения компании «Алроса-Газ», а также строительство магистрального газопровода' as TWO SEPARATE cost/scope line items within Inter RAO's own project budget -- i.e. Inter RAO/Novolenskaya TES LLC is paying for and building the trunk pipeline as its own asset, distinct from (though connecting to) Alrosa-Gas's field infrastructure. (5) bigpowernews.ru/TASS (2026-05-12, url_verifier ok:true, name_found:true): reports the SZPK (capital-investment-protection agreement) signed by 'ООО «НоволенскаяТЭС» (дочерняя компания ПАО «Интер РАО»)' [OOO Novolenskaya TES, a subsidiary of PAO Inter RAO] explicitly covers, as part of the protected investment scope, 'для газоснабжения станции строится более 200 км газопровода' (more than 200 km of gas pipeline being built for the station's gas supply) -- i.e. the entity signing federal investment protection FOR the trunk pipeline is Novolenskaya TES LLC/Inter RAO, not Alrosa-Gas. Given five independent, dated sources (2024-2026) all consistently drawing this same builder/owner line between the UKPG+local distribution (Alrosa-Gas) and the trunk transmission pipeline (Novolenskaya TES LLC/Inter RAO), this is a high-tier, well-corroborated attribution concern, not a single-source guess. Recommend Owner1 -> 'Novolenskaya TES LLC', with a ResearcherNotes flag that its own majority shareholder (99.9%%, per EGRUL via peretok.ru) is AO 'Inter RAO - Elektrogeneratsiya'.

resolutions.recommendation: Keep StartYear1=2028 as recorded -- it is the sponsor's (Inter RAO's) own stated commercial-operation target and the figure most consistently repeated across sources -- but add a ResearcherNotes caveat documenting the sourced 2029 alternative from RF Government statements.
resolutions.researcher_notes: A genuine, sourced date discrepancy exists and should not be silently dropped. neftegaz.ru/886763 (2025-04-17) states this explicitly in one place: 'По информации на сайте Интер РАО, начало поставки мощности на оптовый рынок... намечено на 1 июля 2028 г. Однако в сообщении правительства РФ указывается, что строительство ТЭС и МГП предполагается завершить в 2029 г.' (Per Inter RAO's own site, commercial power supply is targeted for 1 July 2028; however, an RF Government statement indicates construction of the TES and the trunk gas pipeline is expected to complete in 2029.) 1prime.ru (2026-08-06) reports Inter RAO reaffirming, even after a 31%% cost revision, that the update 'не приведет к корректировке нормативного срока начала поставки мощности' (will not require adjusting the normative start-of-power-supply date) -- implicitly reaffirming 2028 as the still-current sponsor target as of August 2026. Given 2028 is (a) the sponsor's own repeatedly-reaffirmed figure, (b) the figure already recorded and sourced to peretok.ru, and (c) still being reaffirmed as of the most recent (2026-08) evidence, recommend keeping StartYear1=2028 rather than changing to 2029, but flagging the government-sourced 2029 figure as a documented alternative in case GEM's convention favors the more conservative/government-sourced estimate.
